intro: Construction laborers coordinate with crews, run equipment and keep a site moving. The closest of the 25 careers below is surface mining excavating and loading machine operation, with a 90% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $57,430, which is 22% more than the $47,120 construction laborers earn.
why_it_works: A day on site means hauling materials, operating tools and machines, and watching for hazards while working with a crew. O*NET rates coordination and operation and control at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Equipment operation, rigging and mining work use the same physical and machine skills. All 25 matches need no extra education. The skills to grow are quality checks and troubleshooting.
tips: Get certified on one machine, such as a loader or crane; operators earn more than general laborers.
Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers earn $95,320, which is 102% more, through paid apprenticeships.
Riggers earn $62,640, or 33% more, and are a 76% match with no extra schooling.

faq.q: What jobs can former construction laborers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are surface mining excavating machine operators (90%), helpers for brick, stone and tile setters (86%) and Riggers (76%), based on O*NET 31.0. Hoist and Winch Operators are also 75% matched and earn $56,450, which is 20% more than the $47,120 laborer median.

faq.q: Which careers for construction laborers pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more than construction labor. Power-line installers earn $95,320 (102% more), mining roof bolters $78,540 (67% more) and rail-track equipment operators $70,070 (49% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most train on the job or through apprenticeships.

faq.q: Do construction laborers need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than construction laborers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 71% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so certifications matter more than degrees.

faq.q: What skills should construction laborers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, troubleshooting, judgment and decision making and operation and control. Coordination already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to run and fix machines is the main step toward better pay.
